definition: the commander of a fleet or a navy
hook: Admiral is an Arabic title that European sailors mistook for a rank.
modernAnchor: Gold braid, a captain's hat, a fleet on the horizon. We call that person an admiral.
journey: Arabic amir meant commander, and it was attached to many offices. Amir al-bahr was the commander of the sea.
Crusaders and Mediterranean traders met Arab fleets and borrowed the title for their own naval leaders.
In Latin and French the al- was taken for part of the word itself, giving amiral.
Spelling later shifted again to admiral, and the commander of the sea became a rank in every navy.
